Given the general preference for y, it's highly likely y will fill up quickly. If y fills up before I get matched, my obtainable set becomes {w, x, z}. In this case, w is the best option ($70).

However, if y *doesn't* fill up, I will get matched to y ($45). If I rank y first, I will go to y if it's available, which is good. But if y fills up, I'll fall back to w (since I'm first priority there) and get $70.

Ranking w first doesn't change my obtainable set. It *only* determines where I go if both w and y are available. Ranking y first doesn't change my obtainable set either.

Since most applicants prefer y, it's likely to be competitive. I'm 1st priority at w, which is a safe bet. Therefore, I should rank w first to secure a good outcome if y is oversubscribed. Then rank the others based on value.
